evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> let lastDay = DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(...)) lastDay.AddDays days
| true, days when days >= 1 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new due-date rule (end of month plus N days) and the words for the terms are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). Validating and parsing the form value is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). Storage only maps the new case to JSON and back. Tier 3 and Tier 4 are not touched, so nothing outside Tier 1/2 decides a domain rule.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no clock, randomness, I/O or persistence. The date arithmetic is pure and uses the issue date passed in. Storage encoding is a pure JSON mapping. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code is touched.

evidence.quote: | true, days when days >= 1 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))
| true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(Net days))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The day-range limit 1..365 is written as a literal in two branches, the existing Net branch and the new EOM branch, instead of being defined once. The copies agree, so this is restated but not drifting. The 'Net {days} EOM' wording appears in both Documents.termsText and Invoicing.termsWords. The termsWords copy is the audit-trail text and follows the existing pattern of separate wording for each. The two agree.

evidence.quote: | DayOfNextMonth day -> let next = DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, 1).AddMonths 1 DateOnly(next.Year, next.Month, day)
| true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording (dayOfNextMonthText) are in Summa.Ledger. Input validation (1 to 28) is in Summa.Web.Engine. Storage only maps the case to JSON. Nothing in Tier 3 or Tier 4 decides a domain rule.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effects. The due-date calculation and ordinal text are pure functions, and the storage change is a pure JSON mapping. Nothing outside the existing structure is touched.

evidence.quote: | true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))
| "day-of-next-month" -> closed [ "day"; "kind" ] value |> Result.bind (fun () -> integer "day" value |> Result.map DayOfNextMonth)

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The ordinal text has one definition, dayOfNextMonthText, which both termsText and termsWords use. The 1..28 limit lives only in the Engine parser. The storage decoder and dueDate do not check it, so a stored day of 31 would make DateOnly throw. This is a missing check, not a second definition. The 365 limit is now literal in three branches, up from two. The copies agree. The 'Net {days} EOM' wording is still written in both termsText and termsWords, as in change set 1.
